sources.retirement_age: Old-age pension (vejez) from 65 under the Ley del Seguro Social (IMSS; cesantía en edad avanzada from 60) and the Pensión para el Bienestar de las Personas Adultas Mayores from 65 (women from 63 in the phase-in of 2025-26; IMSS, https://www.imss.gob.mx/node/1217 and the search digest at https://www.adn40.mx/mexico/2026-07-21/es-oficial-estas-son-las-semanas-cotizadas-obligatorias-para-jubilarte-en-julio-2026/ ; pages not opened: to confirm). One age is used for everyone: 65. Since 2026-10-08 people here stop work at ages of their own, drawn from labour_force_share_by_age; this age is still the one the profile's other figures turn on (the retired's savings, the end of the payments for those out of work, a retirement fund's access) and the top of the working ages the measures use. The pension's age is the payment's own (support.payments).
sources.labour_force_participation_bps: Placeholder: the share of working-age adults (18 to 64) in the labour force, 67%. ENOE Jalisco Q1 2026: participation 56.2% of everyone aged 15 and over (men 72.2%, women 41.6%; INEGI, Encuesta Nacional de Ocupación y Empleo (ENOE), Jalisco, primer trimestre de 2026, boletín de indicador 315/26 (26 May 2026), https://www.inegi.org.mx/contenidos/saladeprensa/boletines/2026/enoe/enoe2026_05_Jal.pdf); the working-age share is higher because the base includes the 65+ and students under 18; the 67% is an estimate from that, to confirm against ENOE's age tables. Those outside it (home-making is 33.6% of the non-active in the 2020 census, studying 42.9%) do not look for work.
sources.labour_force_share_by_age: ILOSTAT, 'Labour force participation rate by sex and age (%)', five-year bands (dataflow DF_EAP_DWAP_SEX_AGE_RT, https://sdmx.ilo.org/rest/data/ILO,DF_EAP_DWAP_SEX_AGE_RT/all?startPeriod=2019; the data file opened and these figures read from it, 2026-10-08), persons, Mexico, national, annual 2025, from INEGI's Encuesta Nacional de Ocupación y Empleo: ages 25 to 54, 76.948%; 55 to 59, 66.947%; 60 to 64, 49.378%; 65 and over, 25.157%. National, not Jalisco (no table by age for the region was found); not checked against INEGI's own table (to confirm). How it is used: the first band is the reference; someone in the labour force stops work at the start of a later band with the chance these shares give, and those still in at the last band never stop. The survey's last band is open (65 and over), so nobody is drawn to stop after 65, and those who work on are older on average than they are in fact: to split when the shares at 65 to 69, 70 to 74 and 75 and over are opened. The profile's own participation figure (labour_force_participation_bps) still says how many are in the labour force at the reference ages; this curve says only how that share falls with age.
sources.tenancy: Código Civil del Estado de Jalisco, title on leases (arrendamiento): a rent may be raised once a year, by notice, so the tenant can agree or object; a legal extension (prórroga) of up to a year is regulated and rent may rise by up to 10% in it if the landlord shows rents in the zone rose as much (summarised by the search at https://leyes-mx.com/codigo_civil_jalisco/2028.htm ; the article numbers and the notice period were not read: to confirm). rent_review_months 12 follows. rent_increase_notice_days 30 is a PLACEHOLDER (the Code's period was not found). after_fixed_term 'periodic': a tenant who stays on after a fixed term continues month to month (tacit renewal; to confirm in the Code).
sources.tenancy.end_notice_days: Codigo Civil del Estado de Jalisco, art 2035 (https://docs.mexico.justia.com/estatales/jalisco/codigo-civil-del-estado-de-jalisco.pdf, a Justia copy of unchecked date, opened 2026-10-16): a lease of indefinite term (a lease not for a fixed term is one, art 2034) ends on notice given 'de forma indubitable': three months if the landlord gives it and one month if the tenant does, and this cannot be waived. 90 days is the three months. Replaces the example code's 60 days. Also: a tenant who has met all obligations has a right to a one-year extension at the end of the term (art 2044, not modelled), and one who stays on without opposition after the term continues month to month (art 2143: 'periodic' agrees).
sources.tenancy.tenant_notice_days: Codigo Civil del Estado de Jalisco, art 2035 (opened 2026-10-16): the tenant's notice ending an indefinite-term lease is one month: 30 days agrees (the placeholder is now sourced).
sources.town_finance.unpermitted_building_fine: Placeholder: the fine the town's planning law sets for building without a permit, 125,200 pesos: the first profile's figure scaled by the shop-wage ratio, as this profile's approval threshold is. To source from this place's planning law.
sources.values: Placeholder: Schwartz's ten basic values, in the pan-cultural order of importance Schwartz and Bardi found across 56 nations (benevolence, universalism, self-direction, security, conformity, hedonism, achievement, tradition, stimulation, power: 'Value hierarchies across cultures', Journal of Cross-Cultural Psychology 32(3), 2001; to confirm), as importance from 7,000 down to 3,400 basis points, each with a spread of 1,500. To source for this place: the World Values Survey's Schwartz items for Australia (wave 6), rescaled. Carried over unchanged: a cross-national ordering, not a Mexican measurement; a placeholder for Mexico, to replace with a Mexican survey of Schwartz values (for example the World Values Survey wave 7 for Mexico, or the European Social Survey's Portrait Values Questionnaire if run there) when found.
sources.industrial_action: Ley Federal del Trabajo (LFT), title 8 (strikes), art 920 fr III: the strike petition (emplazamiento) must give six days' notice in private firms (ten in public services); art 930 and following: the headcount (recuento) of workers decides the strike's legality and only the workers of the firm who attend count. The 2019 labour reform requires a vote of the workers for contract matters. Source of the summary: the search result on arts 920-931 (https://mley.mx/LFT/articulo/920/ and https://mley.mx/LFT/articulo/931/ ; pages not opened: to confirm). notice_days 6 follows. ballot_turnout_bps and ballot_pass_bps (5,000 each: more than half of the workers) follow the rule as summarised (the exact threshold in the strike-legality headcount, art 930 fr II, is a majority of the workers: to confirm). paid_during_action false: strikers are not paid wages (a collective agreement can say otherwise; to confirm).
sources.world_price_process: Placeholder: carried over from au-vic-2026 (monthly mean-reverting random moves in world prices; to estimate from INEGI's Índices de precios del comercio exterior).
sources.credit.cash_rate_bps: Banco de México, target for the overnight interbank interest rate: 6.50% (held on 24 September 2026, unanimous; reported by https://www.poresto.com/mexico/2026/9/24/banxico-mantiene-tasa-de-interes-en-650-y-preve-que-inflacion-llegue-a-la-meta-hasta-finales-de-2027.html , a news report of the decision; the Banxico statement itself not opened: to confirm).
sources.credit.funding_spread_bps: Placeholder: what a small bank pays over the policy rate for funding. Banks' spreads in Mexico are wide; 2 points is an estimate, to source from Banxico's Reporte de Estabilidad Financiera.
sources.credit.lending_rate_bps: Organisations: SME loans average about 15.35% a year (Banco de México via a press digest, https://vanguardia.com.mx/dinero/creditos-cada-vez-mas-caros-en-mexico-HE7017966 ; date of the figure not confirmed, 'datos anteriores': to confirm against Banxico's interest-rate series for business credit). People: personal loans at 21% to nearly 30% a year according to Banxico data cited by the press (https://www.merca20.com/?p=12577970 and the Bloomberg Línea / Excélsior reports; not opened); 24% is taken as the middle of that range, a placeholder.
sources.credit.serviceability_buffer_bps: (Left out since 2026-10-09: the serviceability buffer, which stood here as nought for a rule the place does not have. The note is its author's, as written.) Placeholder: Mexican bank regulation (CNBV) has no stress buffer on the rate like Australia's (APRA); set to 0. A gap in the profile structure's meaning: it is a rule, not a figure.
sources.credit.max_repayment_share_bps: Placeholder: the most of a borrower's monthly income a lender lets repayments take (people 30%, a common lending guide; organisations 20% of what comes in), carried over from au-vic-2026. Mexican banks' rule of thumb (payment-to-income of about 30-35% for mortgages) was not found in a source.
sources.credit.arrears_days: Placeholder: a month behind is arrears (a lender's first notice).
sources.credit.default_days: Cartera vencida: a loan is past due after 90 days without payment under the CNBV's Disposiciones de carácter general aplicables a las instituciones de crédito (Criterios contables, Anexo 33; summarised, page not opened: to confirm).
sources.credit.max_months: Placeholder: the longest term for these loans (five years).
sources.credit.reserve: Placeholder: the cash the bank's lending office keeps back, scaled from au-vic-2026's $100,000 by the ratio of shop wages (2.50), rounded.
sources.opening: Placeholder, to source: what each organisation holds on the first day and the least an adult in the labour force has saved; scaled from au-vic-2026's placeholders by the ratio of the two profiles' shop wages (2.50 pesos per Australian dollar) and rounded.
sources.town_finance.parks_per_year: Placeholder: the town's yearly parks line; scaled from au-vic-2026's by the shop-wage ratio (2.50).
sources.town_finance.payment_approval_over: Placeholder: the town's procedure needs the mayor's written approval for any payment over this; scaled from au-vic-2026's by the shop-wage ratio. The municipal council (ayuntamiento) and its treasurer (tesorero) decide this by Ley de Gobierno y la Administración Pública Municipal del Estado de Jalisco; thresholds not found.
sources.retiree_savings: Placeholder: cash savings at retirement, 30,000 to 90,000 pesos. Most of a worker's retirement wealth is in the individual Afore account (not cash), and a majority never contributed (ENOE Jalisco Q1 2026: 48.6% of the employed are informal; INEGI, Encuesta Nacional de Ocupación y Empleo (ENOE), Jalisco, primer trimestre de 2026, boletín de indicador 315/26 (26 May 2026), https://www.inegi.org.mx/contenidos/saladeprensa/boletines/2026/enoe/enoe2026_05_Jal.pdf); the range is an estimate of what a retiree holds as deposits, to source from ENIF 2024 (INEGI/CNBV) and CONSAR.
sources.support.payments: [The pension:] Pensión para el Bienestar de las Personas Adultas Mayores: 6,400 pesos paid every two months in 2026 (up from 6,200 in 2025), universal, from age 65 (https://www.nmas.com.mx/nacional/cuanto-paga-pension-bienestar-2026-nuevo-monto-oficial-aumento-adultos-mayores-mujeres/ and https://expansion.mx/finanzas-personales/2025/12/15/calendario-primeros-pagos-pension-bienestar-2026 ; news reports of the programme's rules, not the DOF/Secretaría de Bienestar text: to confirm). every_days 61 (one two-month period, 365/6). IMSS pensions (cesantía y vejez) are not modelled; only this universal payment is. [The payment to those out of work:] NO EQUIVALENT: Mexico has no national unemployment benefit (only Mexico City's seguro de desempleo, and a partial withdrawal from the Afore account, ley del Seguro Social art 191). Amount set to 0 so nobody receives one; from_age 18 and every_days 14 are neutral values. The closest thing the structure allows; listed as a gap. Source: Ley del Seguro Social, art 191 (partial withdrawal for unemployment from the Afore account after 46 days; summarised only, not opened: to confirm). SHAPE (2026-10-08, track D of docs/design/profile-depth.md): support is now a list of payments, each a rule in three parts: who qualifies, how much, for how long (docs/behaviour/boundary.md); the law is published and the payments office reads it. UN-FOLDED: the payment of nought that stood for no payment to the unemployed is gone (this note: Mexico has no national unemployment benefit), so nobody claims one and none is counted. The pension is as it was: universal, every 61 days.
sources.firm_ownership.forms_bps: Placeholder: how the firms of each kind are held (docs/behaviour/firm-ownership.md). Shops and landlords are small family businesses held closely: ENOE Jalisco Q1 2026: 45.5% of non-agricultural workers are in micro-businesses and 23.5% in small establishments; of the employed, 6.5% are employers and 18.0% are own-account workers (INEGI, Encuesta Nacional de Ocupación y Empleo (ENOE), Jalisco, primer trimestre de 2026, boletín de indicador 315/26 (26 May 2026), https://www.inegi.org.mx/contenidos/saladeprensa/boletines/2026/enoe/enoe2026_05_Jal.pdf); the closely held/outside split is an estimate. Factories: a mix of family firms, branches of firms from elsewhere and a few listed groups; the split 30/50/20 is a placeholder. No source for ownership forms of firms by kind was found.
sources.firm_ownership.closely_held: Placeholder: the shares with one, two, three owning households (85/12/3), carried over from au-vic-2026 with no Mexican figure; owner_wealth_fifth_bps: closely held firms belong mostly to the richest fifth of households, carried over unchanged.
sources.firm_ownership.widely_held: Placeholder: the part of a widely held firm held from outside (80%), carried over from au-vic-2026.
sources.firm_ownership.direct_holders: Placeholder: share of households holding listed shares directly, by fifth of wealth: 0.5%, 1%, 2%, 4%, 9%. Direct share ownership in Mexico is rare (the Mexican stock exchange, BMV, has a small retail investor base); the figures are estimates of that order, not from a source (to source from CNBV or BMV investor statistics, or the ENIF).
sources.retirement_fund: Placeholder, all of it: the retirement fund's rules were modelled on Australian account-based pensions, and these figures are carried over from au-vic-2026. Mexico's system is the Afores (individual defined-contribution accounts run by private administrators supervised by CONSAR, with a guaranteed minimum pension): a fund of this type exists but its parameters (a pension at the rate of the balance, rising with age) are not Mexico's. Use with a world that asks for one only after replacing from CONSAR statistics. IMSS contribution rates, for reference: retiro 2.0% of salary from the employer, cesantía y vejez employer 3.15% rising to 11.875% by 2030 and 1.125% from the worker, under the 2020 pension reform (https://www.elcontribuyente.mx/indicadores/cuotas-imss/ , summary; not opened).
sources.industry: Placeholder: carried over from au-vic-2026 (manufacturing's compensation of employees and intermediate inputs as shares of output; retail's purchases of goods and wages as shares of sales; from ABS input-output tables). Mexican equivalents: INEGI, Matriz Insumo-Producto 2018 and Censos Económicos 2024 (value added and remuneration by sector). Not opened. Retail's labour share of 14% is likely higher in a country with low retail wages; unverified.
sources.prices: Placeholder, all four, scaled so that the town's price level is consistent with its wages (the shop wage here is 2.50 times au-vic-2026's in currency units): an item of goods worth 250 pesos at world prices (the unit the town counts in; au-vic-2026 uses $100); imports 10% dearer (freight and margins); factory inputs 5 pesos a kg; building materials 4 pesos a kg (retail prices of cement, about 4-5 pesos a kg for a 50 kg bag, are the anchor; unverified, to check against the Sistema Nacional de Información de Precios, SNIIM or INEGI's INPC and the construction input price index).
sources.public_finance.income_tax: Servicio de Administración Tributaria (SAT), Resolución Miscelánea Fiscal 2026, Anexo 8 (published in the Diario Oficial on 28 December 2025): annual tariff for individuals (Art. 152 LISR): marginal rates 1.92%, 6.40%, 10.88%, 16.00%, 17.92%, 21.36%, 23.52%, 30.00%, 32.00%, 34.00% and 35.00% above lower limits of 0.01, 10,135.12, 86,022.12, 151,176.20, 175,735.67, 210,403.70, 424,353.98, 668,840.15, 1,276,925.99, 1,702,567.98 and 5,107,703.93 pesos (the fixed fees in the tariff equal the cumulated tax of the brackets below, so marginal rates are equivalent), from https://elconta.mx/tablas-y-tarifas-isr-2026-anexo-8-de-la-resolucion-miscelanea-fiscal-2026/ (a tax-practice site reproducing Anexo 8; the DOF text not opened: to confirm). The employment subsidy (subsidio para el empleo) for low incomes and employees' social-security contributions (IMSS worker share) are NOT modelled; there is no Medicare-type levy, so levy_bps is 0. Employers withhold monthly in Mexico; here they withhold on each pay, reckoned as a year's income. SHAPE (2026-10-08, track E of docs/design/profile-depth.md): the law is now a list of charges, each with what it is charged on, its schedule, its reliefs and whom it is paid to (docs/behaviour/public-finance.md). One charge, the annual tariff as it was. The levy of nought that stood for no levy is gone. Not expressed, as before: the employment subsidy and the worker's social-security share (the note gives no figures).
sources.public_finance.returns: [RECALLED, to confirm] SAT: tax retained from wages is declared and paid by the 17th of the following month (Ley del ISR arts. 96 and 99). The SAT's pages returned nothing; seen on secondary sites. IMSS dues, also by the 17th, are not a charge in this profile.
sources.public_finance.grants_per_resident_per_y: Placeholder: federal and state transfers to municipalities (participaciones, Ramo 28, and aportaciones, Ramo 33: FISM and FORTAMUN) per resident: about 3,000 pesos a year is an order-of-magnitude estimate for a small Jalisco municipality; the amounts by municipality are in Jalisco's Ley de Coordinación Fiscal distribution and the Ramo 33 / Ramo 28 estimates for 2024 (e.g. https://www.zapopan.gob.mx/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/Estimaciones_Ramo_33_y_28_2024.pdf , not opened). Participations are 50.3% and aportaciones 37.7% of Jalisco state income in 2022 (INEGI, Finanzas públicas estatales y municipales, through IIEG: https://iieg.gob.mx/ns/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/Ficha-informativa-Finanzas-publicas-estatales-y-municipales-ingresos-2022-20240515.pdf ; search snippet). FLAGGED FOR THIS PROFILE'S AUTHOR (2026-10-09, the second live check, finding 14): this placeholder is sized to the whole of a municipality's transfers, which there pay for everything it runs. The town generated from this profile runs only waste collection, the upkeep of its parks, hall and roads, a park and some roads a year and a wildlife survey, so its opening budget spends a part of what this grant pays in. When the figure is sourced it should be the grant for the functions the town has, or the source's spending by purpose should give the share.
sources.public_finance.rates_per_resident_per_ye: Derived, with an assumed input: Jalisco's property tax (predial) tariff in the Ley de Hacienda Municipal del Estado de Jalisco / the municipal Ley de Ingresos applies a marginal rate of 0.0002540 to fiscal values from 0 to 776,142.90 pesos (as published for Guadalajara, https://transparencia.guadalajara.gob.mx/sites/default/files/TasasTarifasImpuestoPredial24.pdf ; a small town's schedule differs, not found); at an ASSUMED fiscal value of 500,000 pesos a dwelling that is 127 pesos a year, over 3.27 residents per household (ENIGH 2024 Jalisco): about 38.8 pesos a resident a year. Predial is a small part of Mexican municipal income; the rest is transfers (above).
sources.public_finance.rates_instalments: Ley de Hacienda Municipal del Estado de Jalisco: the predial is assessed and paid bimonthly (six payments; the Ley de Ingresos of each municipality adds discounts for paying in advance), per the schedule published by Guadalajara (https://transparencia.guadalajara.gob.mx/sites/default/files/TasasTarifasImpuestoPredial24.pdf ; summary only, not read in full: to confirm).
sources.public_finance.rates_due_days: Placeholder: an instalment falls due 30 days after its notice.
sources.public_finance.rates_penalty_interest_bp: Placeholder: surcharges (recargos) on late payments. The Código Fiscal de la Federación's rate of 1.47% a month (17.64% a year, simple) is used as a stand-in; the municipal Ley de Ingresos sets its own (to confirm; the monthly surcharge percentages were not found in the Jalisco results).
sources.public_finance.rates_exempt_kinds: Constitución Política de los Estados Unidos Mexicanos, art 115 fr IV inciso c): the municipal property tax exempts only property in the public domain of the Federation, the states and the municipalities, unless used by parastatal entities or by individuals. Here: the clinic's (public), the school's (public) and the police station's. The utility (CFE-type state enterprise selling a service) is NOT exempt. (Provision recalled from the Constitution; the text was not opened in this session: to confirm.)
sources.public_finance.median_house_price: Sociedad Hipotecaria Federal (SHF), Índice SHF de Precios de la Vivienda, second quarter of 2026: Jalisco's average house price 2,107,232 pesos (8th highest among states; +10.13% on a year earlier), reported by IIEG Jalisco, https://iieg.gob.mx/ns/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/reporte_indice_precios_vivienda_mexico_2doT_2026.pdf (search snippet; the report itself not opened: to confirm). An AVERAGE for the whole state, weighted to metropolitan Guadalajara; a small town's median is lower, so this overstates local prices. Used as the median to derive the land value (this less the cost of building a house).
sources.services.waste_per_person_per_day_g: SEMARNAT, Diagnóstico Básico para la Gestión Integral de los Residuos 2020: 0.944 kg of municipal solid waste per person per day, nationally (120,128 tonnes a day; Jalisco 7,961 tonnes a day), as reported by https://apps1.semarnat.gob.mx:8443/dgeia/compartidos/pdf/COM_MET_GENTOTPER.pdf and the search digest; the Diagnóstico itself not opened: to confirm.
sources.services.landfill_levy_per_tonne: Placeholder: Mexico has no landfill levy like Victoria's; what is charged at a sanitary landfill (relleno sanitario) is a gate or tipping fee set by each municipality or concessionaire. 250 pesos a tonne is an estimate of that order; a figure for Jalisco (for example SIMEPRODE, the Jalisco intermunicipal waste body) was not found. To source.
sources.services.council_staff_per_1000: Placeholder: municipal workers per 1,000 residents. INEGI's Censo Nacional de Gobiernos Municipales y Demarcaciones Territoriales 2025 gives the personnel of municipal administrations; the figure for Jalisco was not found. 5 per 1,000 is an estimate; in the town, all of them are its works crew.
sources.services.collect_seconds_per_10kg: Placeholder: a one-driver side-loader lifts up to 6 bins a minute (Bucher Municipal, Sport side loader); with driving between houses, about 1,000 bins a day is taken as a round, and a household's week of waste as about 24 kg: about 12 seconds of work per 10 kg. (A physical estimate carried over from au-vic-2026, not Mexican.)
sources.services.asset_life_years: Placeholder: a park or civic building wears out in 15 years without upkeep (after VAGO, Maintaining Local Roads: spray seals last 10-15 years). (Carried over; not Mexican.)
sources.services.upkeep_hours_per_week_per_asset: Placeholder: a crew member's half a day a week keeps a park or the hall up (mowing, bins, repairs).
sources.services.complain_bps: Placeholder: the chance a week that a household whose waste has gone two weeks uncollected writes to the town. Who reports and who doesn't varies (the service-request literature, e.g. Stowers 2022, State and Local Government Review); a rate is to be sourced.
sources.public_service.wage_per_pay_period: [PLACEHOLDER] 5,800 pesos per 14 days (about 12,600 a month). Estimated from private job listings for auxiliar administrativo in Jalisco (OCC, Cazvid), which show roughly 10,000-20,000 pesos a month; no 2026 municipal tabulador for Jalisco was opened (state tabuladores exist at presupuestociudadano.jalisco.gob.mx, not read). Sits just above the profile's shop wage (5,292.70 pesos), as a clerk's pay would. 2026-10-16 (not applied): nationally 45.7% of men and 48.0% of women in municipal service earned up to 10,000 pesos gross a month in 2024 (INEGI, CNGMD 2025 results, graph 11, https://www.inegi.org.mx/contenidos/programas/cngmd/2025/doc/cngmd_2025_resultados_ve.pdf, opened): bands of all municipal staff including police; 12,600 a month is in the upper half, plausible, not confirmed. Jalisco's state tabulador's host refused the connection. Staff: nationally 1,071,516 municipal staff in 2024, about 8 per 1,000 of about 130 million (population not opened); Jalisco's police 1.6 per 1,000 (Expansion, 20 March 2026, summary).
sources.public_service.staff_per_1000.administra: [PLACEHOLDER] INEGI's Censo Nacional de Gobiernos Municipales y Demarcaciones Territoriales 2025 counts municipal personnel, but the PDF could not be read and the Jalisco split was not found. services.council_staff_per_1000 already sets 5 per 1,000 for the works crew; municipal administration (offices, registry, planning) is estimated at 3 per 1,000 (to confirm).
sources.public_service.staff_per_1000.courts: [PLACEHOLDER] Estimated, not sourced. Jalisco's first-instance civil courts (juzgados de primera instancia, Supremo Tribunal de Justicia) have a judge plus about 8-10 staff each; at one court per roughly 60,000 residents that gives about 0.15 per 1,000 (to confirm from INEGI's Censo Nacional de Impartición de Justicia Estatal 2025, Jalisco ficha at iieg.gob.mx, not opened). 2026-10-16 (not applied): Jalisco's state judiciary had 3,383 people in 2024 (2,580 in the courts, 803 administrative) in 302 courts, 0.40 per 1,000 (0.31 courts only) over 8.37 million, for all matters (criminal, family, appeals) (IIEG ficha on the INEGI census, opened): 2 to 2.7 times 0.15, but the civil share is unknown, so it stays.
sources.public_service.staff_per_1000.oversight: [PLACEHOLDER] Estimated. Consumer conciliation (PROFECO delegation) and the state human-rights/ombudsman body (CEDHJ) are small and regional; about 0.04 per 1,000 for both together. No staffing figure opened (to confirm).
sources.public_service.staff_per_1000.elections: [PLACEHOLDER] Estimated from the permanent staff of the state electoral institute (IEPC Jalisco) and the INE district office, a few hundred people for about 8.5 million residents: about 0.03 per 1,000. Not opened (to confirm).
sources.public_service.staff_per_1000.land_regis: [PLACEHOLDER] Estimated. Jalisco's Registro Público de la Propiedad y de Comercio has regional offices; staff of the order of 600 for 8.5 million residents would give 0.07-0.08 per 1,000. Not opened (to confirm).
sources.public_service.staff_per_1000.press: [PLACEHOLDER] A local newspaper's editorial staff of about 10 for a town of 100,000 would be 0.1 per 1,000. Rough, no source opened.
sources.public_service.staff_per_1000.banking: [PLACEHOLDER] Estimated. Mexico has about 10-12 bank branches per 100,000 adults (CNBV, to confirm) with about 8-10 staff each, plus a share of back-office: roughly 0.9 per 1,000. Not opened.
sources.public_service.staff_per_1000.utilities: [PLACEHOLDER] Estimated. Water utility (SIAPA or a municipal organismo operador) staff of about 0.8 per 1,000 served plus CFE retail/customer service of about 0.4 per 1,000: 1.2 together. Not opened (to confirm).
sources.public_service.staff_per_1000.union: [PLACEHOLDER] Estimated, not sourced. Mexican unions are mostly sector or company unions with few paid officers locally; 0.08 per 1,000 (about 8 in a town of 100,000).
sources.public_service.licences.payment_system: [PLACEHOLDER] 150 pesos per resident per year (15,000 centavos). Estimated from the order of cost of a core-banking and payment platform for a small regional bank (low millions of pesos a year for tens of thousands of customers). No vendor price opened (to confirm).
sources.public_service.staff_per_1000.property_m: [PLACEHOLDER] Carried over unchanged to every profile: property managers (people who run let homes for their owners) at about one to every 100 to 150 let homes is an industry rule of thumb (to confirm, not opened); a town here has about 380 homes for 1,000 people, so about 3 per 1,000 residents. A manager looks after the letting offices of several landlords.
sources.public_service.staff_per_1000.audit: [PLACEHOLDER] Estimated from the real audit office headcount over the population it serves: Auditoria Superior del Estado de Jalisco (ASEJ, about 400 staff, a guess) plus a share of the Auditoria Superior de la Federacion (about 1,800 staff from memory, for federal money in the state) over about 8.5m residents in Jalisco: about 0.05. From memory, not opened (to confirm).
sources.audit.office: [MIXED] Auditoria Superior del Estado de Jalisco (municipal and state accounts) and the Auditoria Superior de la Federacion (federal money and participaciones), under Constitution arts 79 and 116 and the state's audit law. Named from memory, not opened (to confirm). The neutral name is the platform's.
sources.audit.answer_within_days: [PLACEHOLDER] The audit laws let the audit office require information within a fixed period; the number of days was not opened; 15 days is an estimate (to confirm).
sources.audit.report_within_days: [PLACEHOLDER] The annual public account is delivered to the state congress after the year's end and the audit office's individual reports follow in the next year; 180 days is an estimate from memory (not opened; to confirm).
sources.audit.bodies: [PLACEHOLDER] Periods: decisions every 90 days (a quarter) and accounts every 180 days (an interim, half-yearly examination between the annual audits, so that a year of the run holds two), in line with annual financial audit under INTOSAI ISSAI 1000/2000 and an audit sample of 15% of the period, at least 6 and at most 25 decisions, a size chosen for a town of 1,000 to 100,000 under ISA 530 audit sampling (not opened; to confirm). The support office is the outside world's, so only its decisions are checked; the town finance office is checked on accounts. The chosen sample share is the platform's, not the law's.
sources.public_service.appointed_by: [PLACEHOLDER] Who fills the post of a public body when none of its own staff is left: the town's council, which seconds one of its own staff to it, as a local government assigns officers to bodies it runs. Real places mostly give these appointments to a state body, a minister or a board, none of which the town models, so the council stands in for them (to confirm per place). The paper, which the town keeps on a grant as it keeps the courts, is counted with them (2026-10-25; WM-7). Bodies run on their own account (the bank, the union, landlords, shops) are not covered: their owners or members would appoint, and no owner's or member's office exists to do it.
sources.unions.membership_bps: Placeholder: union membership of employees by industry. No sector split for Mexico was found: about 12% of wage-and-salary workers are union members nationally (secondary report, 'alrededor de 12%', INEGI ENOE-based; https://www.tusbuenasnoticias.com/noticias/opinion/2025/09/08/50130-sindicatos-estan-en-extincion ; not opened) and 22.3% in Nuevo Leon in 2023 (Coparmex via Milenio). 'other' = 12% (the national rate); manufacturing 15%, retail 5%, construction 5% and public administration 35% are estimates that follow the usual ranking (public sector far above private) and are NOT sourced. To replace with INEGI's ENOE tables on union membership by sector.
sources.unions.dues_per_month: Placeholder: about 150 pesos a month (roughly 1.5% of a monthly wage of 10,000 pesos; Mexican unions commonly take 1% to 3%; not sourced).
sources.unions.resignation_notice_days: Ley Federal del Trabajo, art 358: nobody can be forced to join a union or to leave it; a member may resign at any time (taken as effective at once; the article was recalled, not opened: to confirm). Written into each membership as the member's notice.
sources.unions.claim_margin_bps: Placeholder: a union claims the year's rise in prices and 2% more (carried over; the Secretaría del Trabajo's data on revisiones contractuales / salary increases in collective contracts are a calibration target).
sources.unions.meeting_every_days: Placeholder: a members' meeting a month.
sources.unions.teaching: The union movement's claim, in words (content for belief). Its members hold it at the start. The same wording as au-vic-2026.
sources.groups.kinds: The kinds of social group (sport; religious; arts; hobby; other recreational interest), carried over from au-vic-2026, which took them from the ABS General Social Survey's categories: no equivalent Mexican survey category list was found (INEGI's ENCUESTA NACIONAL SOBRE USO DEL TIEMPO and the Módulo de Bienestar Autorreportado, BIARE, ask about leisure and social life; not opened). How often each meets and for how long are placeholders; a Catholic parish (the congregation) holds Mass weekly, taken as 60 minutes (to confirm).
sources.groups.taking_part_bps: Placeholder: the share of adults who belong to a group at the start and go to its gatherings, 40%, carried over from au-vic-2026's calibrated value. No Mexican figure for participation in groups was found. After the start, whether anyone goes is theirs.
sources.groups.per_kind_per_1000_people: Placeholder: one group of each kind for every 1,000 people.
sources.groups.leave_notice_days: Placeholder: a member may leave a club or congregation at once.
sources.groups.kinds.teaching: What a group asks people to hold, in its words (docs/design/ai-citizens.md 5). The congregation's stands for the Christian churches together (in Jalisco 89.2% of people are Catholic and 4.7% Protestant or evangelical: Censo 2020, INEGI, Censo de Población y Vivienda 2020, Presentación de resultados, Jalisco, https://www.inegi.org.mx/contenidos/programas/ccpv/2020/doc/cpv2020_pres_res_jal.pdf); one congregation per town is a simplification.
sources.groups.kinds.held_at_start_bps: INEGI, Censo de Población y Vivienda 2020, Presentación de resultados, Jalisco, https://www.inegi.org.mx/contenidos/programas/ccpv/2020/doc/cpv2020_pres_res_jal.pdf: religion in 2020: Catholic 7,448,776 (89.2%), Protestant/evangelical 396,295 (4.7%), no religion 384,118 (4.6%), believers without affiliation 33,125 (0.4%), others 0.3% of 8,348,151. Christian (Catholic plus Protestant) 93.9%. At the start, the congregation's members hold its teaching strongly, and others up to this share hold it less (as in au-vic-2026).
sources.health: The clinic stands for the town's health system (a liberty: a town of 200 has none). doctors_per_1000: 1.2, from the Secretaría de Salud de Jalisco: 1.25 physicians per 1,000 inhabitants (2019) and 1.18 (2022) for the population without social security (https://presupuestociudadano.jalisco.gob.mx/sid/report/pp/18898 and the MIR documents; search snippet, to confirm); the national density is 2.5 per 1,000 (OECD-based, secondary). doctor_wage_per_pay_period: PLACEHOLDER, 30,000 pesos a month (a salaried public-sector general practitioner; not sourced), converted to 14 days. consult_minutes, seek_care_bps, treats and off_work_severities: placeholders carried over from au-vic-2026 (the conditions here are hospital-level, so nearly everyone with one is treated; care shortens them by a fifth; fatal_kept_bps has no effect while conditions don't kill: docs/behaviour/life.md). Health coverage in Jalisco: 69.9% of people affiliated to a health service in 2020, 71.1% of those to IMSS (INEGI, Censo de Población y Vivienda 2020, Presentación de resultados, Jalisco, https://www.inegi.org.mx/contenidos/programas/ccpv/2020/doc/cpv2020_pres_res_jal.pdf).
sources.round: Working hours 9 to 5, five days a week for everyone, shops included. The legal week is 48 hours over six days (LFT arts 61 and 69; ENOE Jalisco Q1 2026 finds a mean of 41 hours worked a week and 61.3% working 35-48 hours, INEGI, Encuesta Nacional de Ocupación y Empleo (ENOE), Jalisco, primer trimestre de 2026, boletín de indicador 315/26 (26 May 2026), https://www.inegi.org.mx/contenidos/saladeprensa/boletines/2026/enoe/enoe2026_05_Jal.pdf), but the one 'work_days' parameter drives work, shops and school alike, and school runs five days; six would put school on Saturdays. Closest allowed: 5 days (a liberty). School 8 to 13 (SEP basic education runs about four and a half to five hours a day in the morning shift; the day length in the SEP calendar was not found: placeholder, to confirm). Travel: off the roads, a 25 m cell on foot in about 18 seconds (walking about 1.4 m/s: Bohannon 1997, carried over from au-vic-2026; to confirm); on a road, 2 seconds (45 km/h under urban limits; carried over); slower across water, wetland and bush (placeholders). Roads budget: placeholder 120 pesos a resident a year (municipal roads in Mexico are paid from FISM/FORTAMUN transfers; the amount was not found).
sources.ownership: house_owner_bps: 58.68% of inhabited private dwellings in Jalisco are owner-occupied (INEGI, Censo 2020, indicator in MIDE Jalisco, https://mide.jalisco.gob.mx/mide/reporte/ficha_indicador/1477 or /1474 ; search snippet: to confirm which of the two ids carries it); flats here are all rented (a liberty), so the same share is used for houses (an understatement of houses owned, since flats are mostly rented). The rest of Jalisco's dwellings are rented, lent by family (prestada) or in other tenure (the shares were not found). mortgage_bps_by_age: PLACEHOLDER, the share of owner-occupiers still repaying a mortgage by the household head's age; far fewer owners have a mortgage than in Australia because most Mexican homes are self-built or inherited (to source from ENIGH 2024 or INEGI's ENVI). mortgage_payment_per_month: PLACEHOLDER 6,500 pesos (to source: INFONAVIT and SHF report average monthly payments). mortgage_rate_bps: an owner-occupier mortgage rate of about 10.2% to 10.4% in 2025-26 (banks' executives in the press: https://forbes.com.mx/?p=1433411 and similar, not opened; range 10-12%). mortgage_years_left: placeholder. market: a 15% deposit (banks ask 10-20%; INFONAVIT lends more; placeholder), costs about 5% (notary, transfer tax ISAI and registration; placeholder, to source from Jalisco's Ley de Hacienda Municipal), 20-year terms (placeholder; bank mortgages run 10-20 years), buy_bps_per_month 50, relist and cut: placeholders as in au-vic-2026.
sources.utilities.water: litres_per_person_per_day: PLACEHOLDER 200 (CONAGUA reports supply per head in Jalisco above 200 l/day; the residential use figure for a small town was not found). price_per_kl: 20.43 pesos per cubic metre, SIAPA's tariff before its 2025 adjustment (SIAPA Guadalajara area; a 28.74-peso fixed tariff was proposed and revoked in 2025; https://www.aztecajalisco.com/local/siapa-no-aumentara-200-la-tarifa-agua-potable-en-el-amg-para-2026/ and https://www.cronica.com.mx/jalisco/guadalajara/2025/07/23/diputados-de-todos-los-partidos-se-oponen-a-nueva-alza-a-tarifas-del-agua-en-2026/ ; snippets, not opened). The real production cost is 24.94 pesos a cubic metre, and homes using up to 25 m3 a month get an 80% discount until 15 December 2026 (the same reports). A small town's water board charges its own tariff, usually lower (not found). service_per_quarter: PLACEHOLDER 300 pesos. The river's inflow, flow and decay are placeholders carried over from au-vic-2026, sized so a small town's draw is a small share of a modest river's water. Bills go to owners.
sources.utilities.energy: CFE domestic Tarifa 1 for 2026: basic block (first 75 kWh) 1.125 pesos a kWh, intermediate (next 65) 1.369, excess 4.004 (https://www.unotv.com/nacional/las-tarifas-domesticas-de-cfe-van-de-1-a-4-pesos-por-kwh-en-junio-de-2026/ ; news digest of CFE's published tariffs: to confirm); Jalisco homes are mostly on tariff 1B with an effective price near 1.15 pesos a kWh (https://www.voltflow.net/blog/costo-electricidad-mexico-por-estado-cfe-2026 , a private blog, not opened). price_per_kwh 115 centavos. supply_per_day 0: CFE has no fixed daily supply charge for homes, only a minimum billed consumption of 25 kWh (the structure's per-day charge cannot express a minimum consumption; a gap). kwh_per_household_per_day: PLACEHOLDER 6 (about 180 kWh a month for a household in a temperate state; not sourced). grid_price_per_kwh 100: PLACEHOLDER, set just under the retail price so the retailer is not made to sell below cost; in fact CFE sells to homes far below the cost of supply and the Treasury pays the difference (a subsidy the structure cannot express; a gap). grid_emissions_g_per_kwh: 444, the emission factor of the National Electric System for 2024 (0.444 tCO2e/MWh), determined by the Comisión Reguladora de Energía and published by SEMARNAT on 28 February 2025 (https://www.hklaw.com/-/media/files/insights/publications/2025/03/mexicoenvironmentalinsights_march2025_en.pdf ; law-firm digest of the notice, not opened: to confirm).
sources.climate: Weather drawn for each run (docs/behaviour/weather.md). rain_by_month_bps: monthly rainfall at Ciudad Guzmán, Jalisco, climate normals 1991-2020, mm: Jan 28, Feb 11, Mar 11, Apr 2, May 26, Jun 117, Jul 145, Aug 160, Sep 153, Oct 77, Nov 23, Dec 8 (CONAGUA / Servicio Meteorológico Nacional normals as reported by https://www.climate-zone.com/climate/mx/ciudad-guzman/ ; a climate website, SMN tables not opened: to confirm; the station is the nearest well documented, not the town's; Tecolotlán and Ameca, the other towns checked, have 903 and 924 mm a year against 761 here). The river's inflow is taken to follow rainfall with a lag of about a month (each month's flow is half this month's rain and half last month's), so the river runs low in spring and high in August to October: the lag is a PLACEHOLDER. storm_*: PLACEHOLDER, a heavy-rain spell in about one month in seventeen (a year-round figure, though in fact storms and hurricanes strike from June to October; the structure has no seasonal storm chance, a gap); in 2025, 9 of Jalisco's 125 municipalities asked for an emergency declaration from rain, floods or earthquakes (reports at https://www.aztecajalisco.com/local/sismos-y-lluvias-provocaron-desastres-en-estos-municipios-jalisco-en-2025 ; not opened). drought_*: PLACEHOLDER, a drought begins in about one year in ten (to calibrate against the Monitor de Sequía de México, CONAGUA SMN). summer_months [4, 5, 6]: the hot dry months before the rains (April to June are the hottest in the Jalisco highlands; to confirm against the SMN normals). heatwave_*, heat units, illness per unit and warning lead: PLACEHOLDERS carried over from au-vic-2026.
sources.hazards: Floods, placeholders carried over from au-vic-2026, sized against the river as modelled (about 9,000 kL a 25 m cell in the usual flow). A flood-zone figure for the town was not found; Jalisco's emergency declarations from floods (Tlajomulco, Tlaquepaque, Chapala, 2025) show that urban flooding is real but are not hazard thresholds.
sources.crime: Crime (world-expansion 7.2), deliberately rare and driven by circumstance only (Becker 1968; Cohen and Felson 1979). take_bps_per_month_in_need, caught_bps_reckoned and take_quantity: placeholders carried over. detection_bps: PLACEHOLDER 1,000 (10%): of crimes in 2024, 93.2% were not reported or got no investigation file (INEGI, ENVIPE 2025, national, https://www.inegi.org.mx/contenidos/programas/envipe/2025/doc/envipe2025_jal.pdf for Jalisco, which has the lowest hidden-crime figure; Jalisco's victimisation prevalence was 24,179 victims per 100,000 in 2024); the share of investigations that identify who is lower than in Australia, and no figure was found; 10% is an estimate. police_per_1000: 1.6 municipal police per 1,000 inhabitants in Jalisco in 2025 (INEGI, Censo Nacional de Gobiernos Municipales y Demarcaciones Territoriales 2025, as reported by https://politica.expansion.mx/mexico/2026/03/20/municipios-sin-policias-mexico-inegi-2025 ; one in five municipalities nationally has no police; the report itself not opened: to confirm). officer_wage_per_pay_period: PLACEHOLDER, 13,000 pesos a month (to source from Jalisco municipal pay tables). investigation_hours: placeholder.
sources.justice: Placeholder: the town's court is a first-instance civil court (juzgado de primera instancia / juzgado municipal) under the Poder Judicial del Estado de Jalisco. hearing_after_days 60, pay_within_days 30, challenge_bps 2000, apply_bps 1500, apply_after_days 30: no timing or case-rate figures for Jalisco courts were found (INEGI, Censo Nacional de Impartición de Justicia Estatal, would give them; not opened).
sources.elections: Constitución Política del Estado de Jalisco: municipal presidents (presidentes municipales), councillors (regidores) and syndics are elected for three years, starting on 1 October of the election year, re-electable once for the next period (https://mexico.justia.com/estatales/jalisco/constitucion-politica-del-estado-de-jalisco/titulo-septimo/capitulo-i/ ; and the 2024 election summary at https://www.milenio.com/politica/elecciones ; search results, text not opened: to confirm). The mayor is elected by relative majority of a slate (plurality), with the councillors on the same slate: the structure has a single mayor, a simplification of the slate (a gap). turnout_bps: 52.84% of the electorate voted in Jalisco in the 2024 elections (state level; the 2024 municipal turnout by town was not found). stand_bps and news_readers_bps: placeholders carried over. In 125 municipalities the presidency was filled in 2024 (the local-paper readership has no Mexican source).
sources.education: school_ages [3, 17]: compulsory schooling runs from preschool at age 3 to upper secondary (media superior) at 17-18 (Constitución art 3, as amended 2019; recalled, not opened: to confirm the age bounds). school_days_per_year: 185, the SEP calendar for 2025-2026, published in the Diario Oficial (https://www.elimparcial.com/mexico/2025/06/09/sep-ya-publico-su-nuevo-calendario-escolar-oficial-del-ciclo-2025-2026-y-estas-son-las-fechas-de-inicio-y-fin-de-las-clases-asi-como-los-dias-festivos-y-otros-dias-inhabiles/ , a news report of the calendar). students_per_teacher: PLACEHOLDER 22 (SEP's 'Principales cifras del sistema educativo nacional' gives students per teacher by level and state; basic education is near 22 nationally; not opened: to confirm). hours_per_day: PLACEHOLDER 5 (a morning shift). teacher_wage_per_pay_period: PLACEHOLDER, 14,000 pesos a month for a basic-education teacher (SEP salary tables not opened). attainment: INEGI Censo 2020 Jalisco, population aged 15 and over, 6,193,111 people: 2.9% illiterate, 8.9% without primary, 18.0% without secondary (education lag: https://comsoc.udg.mx/printpdf/69189 ; derived: less than primary 11.8% (illiterate plus without primary), primary complete without secondary 18.0%); average schooling 9.9 years (INEGI, Censo de Población y Vivienda 2020, Presentación de resultados, Jalisco, https://www.inegi.org.mx/contenidos/programas/ccpv/2020/doc/cpv2020_pres_res_jal.pdf). The split of the remaining 70.2% into secondary complete (27%), upper secondary (25%) and higher education (18.2%) is a PLACEHOLDER chosen so that the mean is 9.9 years. return_per_year_bps: derived from ENIGH 2024 Jalisco: average quarterly monetary income by schooling: up to primary 21,072 pesos, secondary 26,963, upper secondary 32,402, professional (higher education) 59,573 (INEGI, Encuesta Nacional de Ingresos y Gastos de los Hogares (ENIGH) 2024, presentación de resultados, Jalisco (July 2025), https://www.inegi.org.mx/contenidos/programas/enigh/nc/2024/doc/enigh2024_ns_presentacion_resultados_jal.pdf, page 15): ln(59,573 / 21,072) over 10 more years of school is 10.4% a year. max_years 20: postgraduate (income 122,120 pesos; page 15).
sources.nature: Nature (docs/design/world-expansion.md 2). The town is modelled in the highlands of central-western Jalisco (the Sierra de Amula and Valles region: pine-oak and tropical dry woodland on the slopes, thorn scrub (matorral subtropical), grazed grassland, maize and agave farmland, wetland and gallery woodland on the river), where annual rainfall is 760-920 mm (see climate). cell_m: a cell is a 25 m lot. The landscape around the town (margin_cells, block_cells, shares_bps 30/15/20/30/5, woodland_patches), the covers' succession (cleared land to grassland in a year; scrub to woodland in about 40), the pollution figures, survey_hours_per_ha and survey_staff are PLACEHOLDERS carried over from au-vic-2026 (the land-cover shares of the town's municipality are in INEGI's Uso del suelo y vegetación, Serie VII; not opened). spin_up_years: nature is run alone this long before the start so it begins in its own balance (as ecological and climate models spin up).
sources.nature.species: ALL FIGURES ARE PLACEHOLDERS: no density, home range or population-dynamics figure was looked up for these species. The species are real and live in that region (to confirm ranges against CONABIO and the NOM-059-SEMARNAT-2010 list): Collie's squirrel, Sciurus colliaei, a tree squirrel of the Pacific slope woodlands and dry forests of western Mexico; the Montezuma leopard frog, Lithobates montezumae, a frog of ponds and wet meadows of the central Mexican plateau (listed under special protection in the NOM-059 list, as recalled; not opened: to confirm); and the vermilion flycatcher, Pyrocephalus rubinus, a conspicuous common bird of scrub, farmland and river edges, the common control as the fairy-wren is in au-vic-2026. Densities (0.5 squirrels a hectare of woodland; 60 frogs a hectare of wetland; 1 flycatcher a hectare of scrub), home ranges and the growth, mortality and dispersal rates are carried over by ecological role from au-vic-2026's squirrel glider, growling grass frog and superb fairy-wren, whose own densities were taken from Australian studies. They are not Mexican field values. Squirrels and flycatchers live in family groups or pairs sharing a home range, which isn't modelled, so their breeding threshold is one; frogs breed where at least four share a pond (home range half a hectare). To replace each with a published field study.
sources.automation: (PB-6) The outside world's offers of systems to businesses (docs/behaviour/automation.md). Prices are those of vendors in US dollars, converted at an approximate 2026 rate of 18.5 MXN to the dollar (to confirm; the rate is not the place's own and is not read by any code), into the currency's smallest unit; they are the outside world's, held at today's level unless a yearly change is given, like world prices. self-service-point: a bank of self-checkout or self-ordering units: set-up about US$15,000 (a unit's list price runs US$15,000 to 25,000 installed in retail trade reports; to confirm), a yearly licence and support about 16% of it (support contracts run 10 to 20% of the hardware; to confirm), three years' licence, US$3,000 to leave. It does a share of the task 'serve' (scope: placeholder, 30%, in the range of the share of a retail worker's tasks that Eloundou, Manning, Mishkin and Rock 2023 find exposed to current systems; to confirm) in as long as a person takes (placeholder). production-cell: an automated line or cell: set-up about US$90,000 for a cell (the installed cost of an industrial robot system is a few times the robot's price of about US$50,000: International Federation of Robotics, World Robotics; to confirm), a yearly licence and maintenance about 10% of it, five years' licence, a fifth of the set-up to leave; it does 35% of the task 'make' (placeholder) in 70% of a person's time (placeholder). oversight_hours_per_month and error_bps are placeholders (what looking after one costs the buyer's own staff; how often it gets a unit wrong, refunded at the unit's price). case-handling-system: a system that writes an office's routine papers (a rates notice, a permit decision) and records them: set-up about US$40,000 and a yearly licence of 30% of it (a public-sector case-management system's price; placeholder, to source), three years' licence, a fifth of the set-up to leave; it writes them in 15% of a clerk's time (placeholder) and can do 60% of them (placeholder, in the range Eloundou et al. 2023 give for clerical work; to confirm). Mistakes: 2% of papers (placeholder; automated administration's error rates are a documented risk: Michigan's Auditor General found most fraud determinations of its unemployment system wrong, 2016 (to confirm)).
sources.automation.price_fall_bps_per_year: 0: the outside world's prices for systems are held at today's level (the default); a scenario (worlds/scenarios/falling-system-prices.yaml) gives a yearly fall, with its basis.
sources.automation.firms: (PB-6) How a business weighs a system (docs/behaviour/automation.md). payback_months: the months over which the costs of changing (set-up, exit) must be repaid, 24 for a small business and 36 for a large one (ten staff or more): placeholders, in the range firms report requiring for equipment of two to three years (Graham and Harvey 2001, 'The theory and practice of corporate finance', Journal of Financial Economics; to confirm). hurdle_bps: the margin by which the saving must beat the cost, 20% (placeholder, a margin of safety for a manager's own estimate being unsure). reference_bps: each business already using it that the vendor names eases the hurdle by 2 points, never below nothing (Mansfield 1961, 'Technical change and the rate of imitation', Econometrica; Griliches 1957; Rogers 2003: uptake follows how many have taken it up; the size is a placeholder). on_cost_bps: what staff cost beyond their wage, 0: the world models no employer's charges beyond the wage and redundancy pay. most: the most systems of one kind it takes at once (placeholder).
sources.automation.procurement: (PS-1) Placeholder: no figure was found for this place; a threshold of US$100,000 converted at the approximate rate, in the range of national thresholds for services (to source).
